title: Make Sure You Are Not a Pain in the Neck (part 1)
main_content:
A pain in the neck is a common complaint.

“Pain in the neck” is also a common expression in American English. We use this expression to describe something or someone that gives you an irritated, uncomfortable feeling.

You know, like the couple that comes into a movie theater late. They take off their coats and bags, blocking people’s view . Then as they eat popcorn loudly, they begin talking.

“This movie better be as good as the book,” one says.

“I know,” says the other.  “We paid a lot for these tickets!”

And so did everybody else! And the audience wants to enjoy the movie, not listen to these two pains in the neck.

This expression is not used only for people. Certain activities can be a pain in the neck.

For some, washing the dishes is a pain in the neck. Maybe for you, attending long, boring meetings at work is a pain in the neck.

[This article is divided into 2 parts! Read part 2 tomorrow!]

questions.question: What do we use the expression “pain in the neck” to describe?
options: Something that requires a lot of effort and time
Something or someone that gives an irritated, uncomfortable feeling
A physical ailment that needs medical attention
An object that causes inconvenience in daily tasks
questions.answer: Something or someone that gives an irritated, uncomfortable feeling

questions.question: What do the people in the cinema want to do instead of listening to the two people who are pains in the neck?
options: Discuss the plot of the movie loudly
Share their own popcorn with the couple

questions.question: Is the expression used only for people?
options: Yes, it exclusively refers to annoying individuals
No, it can also refer to certain activities
No, it only applies to events and situations
Yes, it describes a specific type of personality
questions.answer: No, it can also refer to certain activities
